instrument_name: 34 Pa. Code 231.36 Statement to employee
authority: Pennsylvania Code (PA Bulletin)
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer shall furnish each employee a statement with every payment of wages listing hours worked, rates paid, gross wages, allowances claimed as part of the minimum wage, deductions and net wages. Page current through 56 Pa.B. 5370 (2026-08-08). Minimum Wage regulation; the WPCL itself (Act 329 of 1961) has no pay-statement section.

instrument_name: Wage Payment and Collection Law, Act 329 of 1961 (43 P.S. 260.1 ff.)
authority: Pennsylvania General Assembly
figure_or_rule_carried: Full act read locally: Sec. 3 regular payday, Sec. 4 notification of paydays and rates, Sec. 6 written notice of conceded wages in a dispute. No itemized pay-stub requirement in the act (zero hits for statement/itemiz).

instrument_name: Pennsylvania Prevailing Wage Act, Act 442 of 1961 (43 P.S. 165-1 ff.)

instrument_name: Ohio Revised Code 4113.14 Pay stubs (Pay Stub Protection Act, HB 106)
authority: Ohio Revised Code (Legislative Service Commission)
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer provides a written or electronic statement of earnings and deductions each pay period on regular paydays: employee name and address, employer name, gross, net, amount and purpose of each addition/deduction, pay date and period, and for hourly employees hours, rate and hours over 40 per workweek. Employee requests in writing; employer has 10 days; then report to the director of commerce; notice posting 10 days.

instrument_name: Georgia DOR 2026 Employer Withholding Tax Guide (rev. September 2026)
authority: Georgia Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Withhold on residents for services inside or outside Georgia (not when outside Georgia and the other state requires withholding) and on taxable nonresidents for Georgia services. Taxable nonresident = regularly engaged in Georgia activity, including those attributing more than 5% of wages or more than 5,000 USD of wages to Georgia. No reciprocity text, no local wage tax, no SDI text, no rounding rule found. The 23-calendar-day-per-quarter exemption seen in search summaries is NOT in the guide text.

instrument_name: NC-30 2026 Income Tax Withholding Tables and Instructions for Employers, Section 5
authority: North Carolina Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Residents: withhold on all wages wherever earned, except no withholding on wages for services in another state if that state requires the employer to withhold. Nonresidents: withhold on any part of wages for services performed in NC; relief from double withholding is the employee residence state job. No reciprocity text and no day or dollar threshold in the publication. Percentage method: withholding rate 4.09% (3.99% plus 0.1%), round to nearest whole dollar.

instrument_name: 446 (Rev. 02-26) 2026 Michigan Income Tax Withholding Guide
authority: Michigan Department of Treasury
figure_or_rule_carried: Michigan employers withhold on nonresidents for work done in Michigan unless covered by a reciprocal agreement; agreements with Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Minnesota, Ohio and Wisconsin. Out-of-state employers with employees working in Michigan must register and withhold. No rounding rule in the guide (zero hits). Withholding calculator at michigan.gov/taxes/business-taxes/withholding/tax-calculator. No payroll service or POA text in the guide.

instrument_name: 5469 (Rev. 05-25) 2026 City of Detroit Income Tax Withholding Guide
authority: Michigan Department of Treasury - City Tax Administration
article_or_section: Who must withhold; rates; due dates
figure_or_rule_carried: Detroit: rate 2.4% residents, 1.2% nonresidents; withhold on residents wherever they work and on nonresidents whose predominant place of employment is Detroit; Form 5527 (DW-4) certificate; monthly return Form 5323 and payment due the 15th of the following month; annual reconciliation Form 5321 for TY2026 due 2027-02-28. Resident working in another taxing city: Detroit rate = 2.4% minus the other city nonresident rate. The other 23 cities are not covered by this guide.
